major: Melody (calm): The middle value of the whole map, as a place on the colour legend. A single line that rises and falls with the overall level.
Harmony (calm): The mix of ranges across the map (the histogram). A chord: thin when the map is of one kind, thicker when it is mixed. It changes only when the mix does.
Bass (standard): How far the map is from normal, or from where this run began when the data has no normal. A low note that sits higher when the map is above normal and lower when it is below.

Hot spots (standard): The largest patches of the highest or lowest range: where they are and how big. One short note a patch. Patches in the west sound in the left ear and patches in the east in the right; bigger patches are louder.

Rhythm (full): The strongest edge in the picture and how much of the picture is edge. An arpeggio that follows the edge from west to east: slow when the picture is smooth, busy when it is full of edges.
Motion (full): How much of the picture moved since the last frame, and which way. A soft pad that opens when there is more movement and leans towards the side the movement goes.
Time (calm): The date. A steady pulse, with a small accent at the start of a new month and a bigger one at the start of a new year.
